author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body_head:
### Why

Currently, custom focus-trapping and scrolling layouts capture keydown events globally. This intercept behavior breaks essential accessibility standards by overriding standard native keyboard controls. For example, when a user is editing text in a `<textarea>` nested inside an overlay modal, pressing the Up or Down arrow keys triggers custom focus-cycling instead of moving the text cursor. Similarly, trying to adjust a range slider or select dropdown inside a scrolling container causes the entire container to scroll instead of modifying the element's value.

This PR introduces a unified, synchronous bypass mechanism to ensure native interactive form elements maintain standard keyboard capabilities, removing duplicate element-sniffing code across the codebase.

---

### Key Changes

#### 1. Introduced Shared Keyboard Utilities
* Created `src/app/core/utils/keyboard-bypass.util.ts`.
* Implemented `isNativeFormField(element)` to identify `<input>`, `<textarea>`, and `<select>` tags that require native cursor and select handling.
* Implemented `isScrollBypassElement(element)` to detect `<select>` elements and `<input type="range">` elements that must ignore keyboard-scroll int
title: Create shared keyboard utilities to restore native form navigation

author: Copilot
body_head:
The `publish-android` job failed when `keytool` could not recognize the decoded keystore. The workflow now handles secrets that contain an extra Base64 layer.

- **Keystore decoding:** Detect Base64 text after the first decode and decode it once more; binary keystores remain unchanged.

```powershell
$nestedBase64 = [System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($keystoreBytes) -replace '\s', ''
if ($nestedBase64.Length -gt 0 -and $nestedBase64.Length % 4 -eq 0 -and $nestedBase64 -match '\A(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{2}==|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{3}=)?\z') {
  $keystoreBytes = [System.Convert]::FromBase64String($nestedBase64)
}
```
title: Handle double-encoded Android signing keystores

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Summary

"Demand hints" on the Schedule page — a Fire-icon button (badge shows hint count) opens a dialog listing class/weekday pairs that consistently over- or under-fill, so staff know where to add a second session and where to trim dead slots.

- `svc.scheduleDemandHints(orgId, tz, weeks=6)`: pulls non-cancelled sessions from the last 6 weeks with a per-session `demand` count (every non-cancelled booking — attended + no-show + booked + waitlisted, so historic demand isn't lost when waitlists expire), groups by `classTypeId` × gym-tz weekday, and emits:
  - `add` — ≥3 runs, avg fill ≥85%: "Avg 110% full — consider adding another Spin on Fridays"
  - `drop` — ≥4 runs, avg fill ≤30%: "Avg 18% full — consider dropping or merging this slot"
- Fill is capped at 100%/session before averaging so one overbooked session can't mask a lukewarm pair; each hint carries the mode start time, session count, and class color for the row.
- Dialog renders rows grouped add-first with green "Add" / amber "Drop" chips and the suggestion sentence; empty state explains the 3-run threshold.

Deterministic heuristic (no AI key needed); it doubles as the data feed if the EE AI insights surface wants it
title: Schedule demand hints — where to add or drop classes

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Summary

`cache_control_injection_points` is LiteLLM's own request field, consumed by its Anthropic transform — but `_prompt_cache_extra_args()` attached it to any model *name* containing "claude", conflating model identity with provider routing. A bare `claude-sonnet-4-5` with `LLM_API_BASE` set (i.e. Claude behind an OpenAI-compatible gateway) is served by the SDK's own OpenAI client, which forwards unknown request kwargs straight into `AsyncCompletions.create()`, so every turn dies before the first token:

```
TypeError: AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'cache_control_injection_points'
```

The gate now asks who actually serves the request, mirroring `StrixProvider._resolve_prefixed_model()` (bare names and `openai/`/`any-llm/` → SDK clients; anything else prefixed → LiteLLM fallback):

```diff
-if not is_claude_model(model_name):
+if not is_claude_model(model_name) or not routes_through_litellm(model_name):
     return None
```

```python
def routes_through_litellm(model_name: str | None) -> bool:
    name = (model_name or "").strip()
    if not name or codex.subscription_model(name):
        return False
    prefix, _, rest = name.partition("/")
title: fix(llm): only attach prompt-cache points on routes LiteLLM serves

body_head:
## Summary

Fix two `Export` edge cases in the storybook example's static mirror, found by Devin Review on the ported copy in go-classic-mpa-sample:

- **Relative `-o` could delete the app's real assets.** `dst := filepath.Join(dir, "static")` stayed relative while `src := b.staticRoot()` is absolute, so `filepath.Rel` failed inside `inside()` and the `dst == src` containment check passed silently — `os.RemoveAll(dst)` then deleted the actual `static/` directory. `Export` now resolves `dir` to absolute up front.
- **A vanished source left a stale mirror.** When `static/` disappeared between exports, `srcOK` went false and the old `out/static` survived. `RemoveAll(dst)` now runs unconditionally (it only skips when `dir` itself is rejected), so the snapshot always mirrors the source.

New regression tests: `TestExportRejectsOutputCoveringStaticSource` (relative `-o` pointing at the package dir must fail, not delete `static/app.css`) and `TestExportDropsStaticWhenSourceGone`.

author: Copilot
body_head:
Three bugs in the deploy/cleanup workflows: missing permission causes 403 on PR comments, `grep` nonzero exit can kill the slug step under `pipefail`, and cleanup derives a different directory name than deploy (leaving stale deployments).

## Changes

- **`deploy.yml` — add `issues: write` permission**
  The PR comment step hits `/issues/{number}/comments`, which requires `issues: write`. `pull-requests: write` alone is insufficient and causes a 403.

- **`deploy.yml` — replace `grep -v '^$'` with `awk 'NF{print}'`**
  Under `bash -e -o pipefail`, `grep` exits 1 when it matches nothing (e.g. `feat/_`), killing the step. `awk` filters empty lines without a nonzero exit.

  ```diff
  - SHORT=$(... | tr -- '-_' '\n' | grep -v '^$' | cut -c1 | tr -d '\n' | head -c 20)
  + SHORT=$(... | tr -- '-_' '\n' | awk 'NF{print}' | cut -c1 | tr -d '\n' | head -c 20)
  ```

- **`cleanup.yml` — align `feat/*` directory derivation with `deploy.yml`**
  Cleanup used an old algorithm (uppercase initials for PascalCase, raw suffix for kebab-case) that diverged from deploy's lowercase-initials scheme, causing cleanup to target the wrong directory. Now both workflows run the identical pipeline.
title: Fix workflow: issues:write permission, grep pipefail bug, cleanup/deploy dir mismatch

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body_head:
### Why
As our core data ingestion, parsing, and migration workflows evolve, manual updates to JSDoc comments are prone to human error. Documentation drift—such as outdated parameter lists or missing return tags—leads to broken compliance guarantees. This is particularly critical for our regulatory GxP-relevant layers, where perfect traceability between code implementation and design documentation is required. 

To eliminate code-review overhead and avoid the maintenance of custom validation scripts, we are introducing automated verification rules directly into our existing linting configuration. This blocks non-compliant code during local development and stops undocumented drift before it reaches the main branch.

### Key Decisions & Rationale
- **ESLint Integration over Custom Scripts:** We chose `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` rather than standalone verification tools. This preserves unified configuration patterns and leverages existing developer tooling.
- **Targeted Directory Scopes:** We specifically scoped these JSDoc rules to target core modules (`src/taskpane/core/**/*.ts` and `src/taskpane/core/**/*.tsx`). This isolates GxP-relevant services while avoiding high-volume rule noise in
title: feat: enforce automated JSDoc compliance in core services

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body_head:
### 💡 What
Optimized `_generate_content` in `jsdoctor/generator.py` by grouping symbols by type in a single pass using `collections.defaultdict(list)` instead of invoking `_get_symbols_of_type` repeatedly over `sorted_symbols`.

### 🎯 Why
Previously, `_generate_content` iterated over `sorted_symbols` multiple times for each symbol type (`CONSTRUCTOR`, `INTERFACE`, `FUNCTION`, `PROPERTY`, `ENUM`, etc.), creating redundant linear scans. Grouping symbols once upfront reduces the filtering overhead from multiple passes down to a single pass while preserving symbol order and type annotations.

### 📊 Measured Improvement
- Baseline (`_generate_content` for 100 runs on 1000 symbols): `50.01s`
- Optimized (`_generate_content` for 100 runs on 1000 symbols): `23.82s`
- **Improvement:** ~2.1x speedup (~52.4% reduction in execution time) for document content rendering.

`printRows` and `printSchemaRows` used hard-coded separators and variable-width columns, making output hard to read when values differ significantly in length.

## Changes

**New helpers (`root.go`)**

**`printSchemaRows`** — same buffering approach; dynamic widths replace the hard-coded `"Name | Type | Mode | Description"` / `"--------------------------------"` strings

```
Name       | Type      | Mode     | Description
--------------------------------------------------

created_at | TIMESTAMP | NULLABLE | Creation timestamp

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Descripcion del cambio

Tres causas reales del total mal sumado en Gestion de Mesas:

1. **La sesion de SQLAlchemy tiene `autoflush=False`** (`app/database.py`). `recalculate_ticket_totals` consultaba `TicketItem` con los cambios todavia pendientes en memoria, asi que al borrar un item la fila seguia existiendo en la base y el total se recalculaba **con el item borrado adentro**: el valor no bajaba. Lo mismo pasaba al mover items entre cuentas (`merge`/`split`), donde el `ticket_id` reasignado aun no estaba escrito.

```python
def recalculate_ticket_totals(ticket, db):
    db.flush()   # los cambios pendientes se escriben antes de sumar
    ...
```

2. **Items anulados que seguian visibles.** Cuando el item ya tenia comanda, borrarlo lo marca `status="cancelled"`; el total lo excluye, pero `get_ticket_response` seguia devolviendolo, asi que en pantalla quedaba la linea con su valor y el total "no cuadraba" con las lineas visibles. Ahora los cancelados no se devuelven. Ademas el filtro usaba `status != "cancelled"`, que en SQL descarta las filas con `status` NULL (items historicos), dejandolas **fuera** del total; ahora se incluyen con `or_(status == None, status != "cancelled")`
title: fix(mesas): recalcular bien el total de la cuenta y eliminar pedidos de verdad

# Branch-Isolated Next.js and Playwright Dual Caching

## Proposed Changes
This PR implements a robust, branch-isolated dual caching strategy in the CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) to drastically reduce pipeline execution times and prevent concurrent branch build interference.

### 1. Playwright Browser Binary Caching
- **Path:** `~/.cache/ms-playwright`
- **Action:** Caches the browser installation directory using `actions/cache@v4`.
- **Logic:**
  - If a cache hit is achieved, runs `npx playwright install-deps` to ensure system dependencies (shared libraries, etc.) are installed on the GitHub Actions runner without redownloading the browser binaries.
  - If a cache miss occurs, falls back to running the full `npx playwright install --with-deps`.

### 2. Next.js Build Cache Preservation

- **Action:** Caches the compilation directory using `actions/cache@v4`.

author: Copilot
body_head:
Addresses three issues: agents visually "teleporting" across the scene during CSV pedestrian scenario playback, a missing purchase (Achats) summary with total revenue (CA) and margin in the Waypoint/Rendement panel, and a missing heatmap of picked-up/checked-out products weighted by margin (€) to surface the most performant zone.

## Agent teleport fix

- Root cause: when the live-tick frame supply stalls long enough (e.g. heavy synchronous work while loading/registering a CSV pedestrian scenario), the render clock hard-snaps forward (`advancePlaybackClock`'s resnap branch) — but per-agent position smoothing had no awareness of this jump, so agents were exponentially smoothed toward their new, far-away target over a handful of frames, looking like a fast dash/teleport across the store (often right-to-left, following the store's flow direction).
- Added `isClockResnap` in `simulationPlayback.ts`, exposing the same resnap predicate `advancePlaybackClock` uses internally.
- `SimulationLayer.tsx` now checks `isClockResnap` before advancing the clock and, when true, clears the per-agent smoothing state (`agentPoses.current`) so agents cleanly reappear at their resynced position instead
title: Fix agent teleport-on-resync + add purchase (CA/marge) totals and pickup-margin heatmap

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Intent

`execute` code written in TypeScript runs the same on a machine (execution context) and with `kody execute --local --code` as it does on Kody cloud.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

Kody cloud accepts TypeScript in `execute` code. The daemon and `--local --code` handed the code to local workerd untouched, so a run that an execution chain routed to a machine failed with `SyntaxError: Missing initializer in const declaration at main.js`. On 2026-11-15, 37 runs on one context failed this way in three minutes. The daemon was on the latest CLI, so this was not an outdated runner.

## Summary

- `runLocalExecute` strips TypeScript from inline `code` with esbuild (`stripLocalUserModuleTypes` in `packages/cli/src/local-bundle.ts`). `--file` already bundled TypeScript. One path covers daemon runs and `--local --code`.
- `verbatimModuleSyntax` keeps every value import, so side-effect imports of `kody:` modules survive.
- A syntax error in inline code is now reported before workerd starts, with file, line and column: `Local execute could not load the module: SyntaxError` followed by `main.ts:1:23: Unexpected end of file`. It is still a run error result, not a thro
title: fix(cli): run TypeScript execute code on execution contexts and --local --code, like Kody cloud

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `fallbacks: [{"primary": ["fb1", "fb2"]}]` never reached `fb2` when `fb1` died mid-stream
- The stream failure was looked up under `fb1`, which has no chain of its own
- On `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` the `fb1` hop was not even watched for a mid-stream failure

How it solves it:

- The lookup now ends with the group the request was originally for
- Already attempted entries are skipped, so `fb1` is not retried
- Refusal and content-filter gates stay closed once every entry was tried
- Every Responses and Messages hop is wrapped the same way the first attempt is

## User Flow

Before: a developer with a two-entry fallback list gets an error on every endpoint even though the second entry is healthy

1. The proxy admin configures `fallbacks: [{"primary": ["fb1", "fb2"]}]` and `[{"anthropic-primary": ["anthropic-fb1", "anthropic-fb2"]}]`
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "primary"` and `"stream": true`
3. `primary` fails, the proxy moves to `fb1`, and `fb1` dies before its first chunk
4. The developer gets back `{"error": {"message": "... upstream died mid-stream", "code": "500"}}`. `fb2` was nev
title: fix(router): walk every entry of a fallback list after a mid-stream failure

body_head:
## What and why The RDF export has long written, for every `port def P`, the `ConjugatedPortDefinition` `~P` the abstract syntax implies, its `OwningMembership` and its `PortConjugation` back to `P`. The native reflective read synthesized none of the three, so a query's `ownedRelationship`, `ownedMember`, `ownedMembership` and `conjugatedPortDefinition` of a port definition disagreed between the native and SPARQL evaluations of the same model (the second of the three `ownedRelationship` families in the qvts cross ledger, after the satisfy subject of #1806). The symbol builder now registers, as the first member of a port definition's scope, a `~P` symbol declared by a `symbols.ImpliedDecl` — a symbols-layer node keyed to the written `port def`, so the AST stays what the parser produced and the implied element is a derived fact over it. author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Summary

**Root cause**: `processPayment()` fired `submitElectronicPayment()` as fire-and-forget (`.then()/.catch()` without `await`). When BILL needed MFA or failed, the error was silently swallowed and the user was told "settled" even though no real funds moved externally.

**Fix**: Payment now **awaits** the BILL transmission and reports the actual outcome:

```diff
- settlementEngine.submitElectronicPayment({...}).then(...).catch(...)
+ var eslResult = await settlementEngine.submitElectronicPayment({...})
+ transmissionStatus = 'transmitted'  // or 'mfa_required' / 'failed'
```

Response now includes `transmission_status`, `payment_confirmed`, and `confirmation_message` so the caller knows exactly whether real funds moved.

**New endpoints**:
- `GET /api/hce/payment-confirmation/:txnId` — polls BILL `ReadEntity('SentPay')` for actual recipient payment status (scheduled/processing/processed/failed)
- `POST /api/hce/retry-transmission` — retransmit after MFA is provided

**Applies to both NFC and QR paths** since both use the shared `processPayment()` function. `processExternalQRPayment()` now returns `transmission_status` and `payment_confirmed` to the frontend.

Link to Devi
title: fix: HCE/QR payments await real BILL transmission with receipt confirmation

### Purpose & Context

This PR resolves layout instability and rendering glitches across three core interface panels: `UniversalStepper`, `DictionarySidecar`, and `SubmissionMetadataView`. 

Previously, these components used manual string interpolation to combine dynamic CSS classes. This approach is highly sensitive to stylesheet load orders and can cause unpredictable styling evaluations and layout shifts in the browser. 

Furthermore, inline style overrides in the stepper component bypassed the theme compiler, making it susceptible to style overriding bugs.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body_head:
**SakJules · Master of Automation & CI/CD.**

🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix Command Injection Vulnerability via `eval()` in Documentation

🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** The documentation and instruction set for the `SakKing-smolagents` persona contained `return eval(expression)` in the example `@tool` implementation for a calculator. In the context of LLM agents, instruction templates and examples are directly loaded into the LLM's context. The agent will likely mimic this exact pattern when generating code for execution, introducing a critical arbitrary code execution/command injection flaw into the agent's actual operational environment.
🎯 **Impact:** If an agent copies this pattern to evaluate math expressions or arbitrary strings provided directly or indirectly by an untrusted source, an attacker could execute arbitrary python code leading to full system compromise.
🔧 **Fix:** Replaced the vulnerable `eval(expression)` with the secure `simpleeval.simple_eval(expression)` and included the necessary `# Requires: pip install simpleeval` and `import simpleeval` statements to prevent user friction. Added this specific threat vector pattern to the Sentinel learning jour
title: 🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix command injection via eval() in SKILL.md documentation

body_head:
`cao-activity.yml` re-downloaded and re-ingested the entire accumulated `gh-aw-logs.jsonl` history on every run via `gh aw logs --cached-jsonl`, wasting work reprocessing already-ingested data. `gh aw logs` now supports `--cached-logs` with a trailing wildcard, which caches results as per-run shards instead of one growing file, enabling incremental collection.

- **Collection step (`cao-activity.yml`)**
  - Seeds a transient shard directory from the cached `gh-aw-logs.jsonl`.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body_head:
🛡️ Sentinel: [HIGH] Fix AI Guard Wrapper arbitrary file overwrite via /tmp symlink

Problem:
The AI guard wrapper (`dot_gemini/config/executable_ai-guard-wrapper.py`) logged debug output to `/tmp/ai-guard-wrapper.log` using a static path when `AI_GUARD_DEBUG` was set. Because `/tmp/` is a shared directory, this created a symlink vulnerability where a local attacker could pre-create `/tmp/ai-guard-wrapper.log` as a symbolic link pointing to a protected file. If the wrapper script was executed by a privileged user, the debug log data would be appended to the target file, resulting in an arbitrary file overwrite.

Change:
Updated the script to log to a secure, user-owned path instead (`~/.local/state/ai-guard-wrapper.log`). We first evaluate the expanded path, ensure the parent directory (`~/.local/state`) exists, and then open the file for appending. This follows XDG directory standards and entirely eliminates the symlink attack vector in `/tmp`.

Currently, the repository tracks compiled Python bytecode (specifically, `tools/__pycache__/compiler_utils.cpython-312.pyc`) and lacks standard ignores for common IDEs, operating systems, and backup file patterns. So the Windows jobs no longer check out at all:

`build-msi.sh` resolves `REPO_ROOT` from its own location, so the flat artifact layout is all it needs; `bash` is
used explicitly because artifacts drop the executable bit. The ubuntu publish jobs keep their checkouts.
`releasing.md` and the changelog fragment describe the new shape. Version stays 0.9.1.

author: Copilot
body_head:
SC2 training could hang after episode 1 during grid search because post-episode replay persistence could block indefinitely, preventing the next episode reset/restart from executing. This change makes replay saving fail-fast instead of stalling the training loop.

- **Replay save is now bounded**
  - `SC2Client.save_replay(...)` executes the underlying PySC2 `save_replay` call in a daemon worker thread.
  - The caller waits up to `_SAVE_REPLAY_TIMEOUT_S` (5s); on timeout it logs and returns `None` (skip replay), allowing training to continue.

- **Error/timeout handling remains non-fatal**
  - Existing behavior of swallowing replay-save failures is preserved.
  - Timeout is treated as another non-fatal replay-save failure mode.

- **Targeted regression coverage**
  - Added a unit test that simulates a slow `save_replay` call and asserts fast return with `None`, guarding against future reintroduction of blocking behavior.

```python
worker.start()
worker.join(timeout=_SAVE_REPLAY_TIMEOUT_S)
if worker.is_alive():
    logger.warning("SC2Client.save_replay timed out after %.1fs; skipping.", _SAVE_REPLAY_TIMEOUT_S)
    return None
```
title: Prevent SC2 training stalls by time-bounding replay saves between episodes

This pull request introduces a hybrid tiered execution model for primality verification and enforces runtime proof-to-code integrity via AST-level drift-detection at startup. Additionally, it bolsters build-time safety by auditing references within the system's trust boundary documentation.

### Why: Key Decisions & Rationale

1. **Eliminating False-Positive Prime Classifications** 
   The mathematical engine previously executed unverified trial-division and probabilistic checks, bypassing the mathematically proven trial-division algorithm. For candidate integers under $2^{64}$ (commonly generated during ray-casting operations), this introduced unacceptable risks of false-positive prime classifications due to unproven mathematical axioms. By implementing a tiered execution path, we route inputs under $2^{64}$ to the mathematically proven trial-division logic while preserving the recursive fallback path for larger candidates—thus maintaining standard performance without sacrificing mathematical rigor.

2. **Mitigating Code-Proof Drift** 
   To guarantee that the running system strictly aligns with verified mathematical specifications, we added an AST-level dr

author: google-labs-jules[bot]

🎯 **What:**
Removed hardcoded "mock-" string fallbacks for all Firebase configuration keys in `frontend/src/lib/firebase.ts`. The configuration now relies strictly on `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_*` variables.

⚠️ **Risk:**
If left unfixed, the application could fall back to using invalid "mock" keys when expected environment variables are absent. This could potentially allow the application to proceed to initialize Firebase with unsafe configuration defaults rather than explicitly failing, which may lead to unhandled errors, bypassed configuration assertions, or unexpected requests using fake keys. 

🛡️ **Solution:**
Removed the `|| "mock-..."` fallback assignments from the `firebaseConfig` object initialization. This ensures that the configuration strictly reflects the environment. If the variables are missing, they remain undefined, causing standard initialization functions to fail securely instead of proceeding with invalid mock data.

## Summary
`BufWritePost` hook: if the buffer has an ancestor dir containing `.autocommit` (cached per buffer in `vim.b.autocommit_root`), run async

```sh
git -C <root> add -- <file> && git -C <root> commit -q -m "[autocommit] save <relpath>" -- <file>
```

Matches the `[autocommit] compile <relpath>` commits from the cp-book contest template (ecnerwala/cp-book#148).

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body_head:
### Summary
This PR addresses a critical performance bottleneck in Phase 1 search processing by replacing expensive runtime factorization (Pollard's Rho) with a pre-computed static lookup table embedded directly into the binary. This change targets the first 250,000 primes, covering the vast majority of standard search operations.

### Rationale
Currently, the engine spends a significant portion of Phase 1 re-calculating cyclotomic factors that are constant for standard search ranges. While the system operates on hardware with 16GB of RAM, this memory is largely underutilized while the CPU is throttled by redundant math operations.

By baking these factors into the executable, we trade a negligible amount of binary size (~5MB) and RAM (~15MB) for a massive reduction in runtime—shifting Phase 1 completion from several hours to under one hour.

### Key Changes

#### 1. Automated Factor Generation (`build.rs`)
The build script now includes a generation phase that produces `cyclotomic_factors.bin`. 
- **Efficiency:** Uses trial division and a deterministic $u128$ Miller-Rabin sieve to keep build times low.
- **Filtering:** Automatically rejects cyclotomic polynomials with prime factors
title: Optimize Phase 1 search with static build-time factor embedding

The failing `e2e` Actions job was caused by a transient `POST /start-session` timeout (`408`) in the session lifecycle suite. That early failure prevented `clientId` initialization and cascaded into broad `404` failures across downstream integration suites.

- **Workflow hardening (targeted retry)**
  - Updated `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml` to wrap `relay/scripts/test-docker.sh` with log capture and conditional retry logic.
  - If the first run fails and logs include the specific `Session › /start-session (v13) › POST /start-session` failure signature, the workflow retries the suite once.
  - Non-matching failures still fail fast with the original exit code.

- **Failure scope control**
  - Retry is intentionally narrow (single trigger pattern, single retry) to reduce noise while preserving signal for unrelated failures.

```yaml
- name: Run live Foundry + relay integration suite
  working-directory: relay
  run: |
    set +e
    LOG_FILE="$(mktemp)"
    bash ./scripts/test-docker.sh 13 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_FILE"
    EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

    if [ "$EXIT_CODE" -ne 0 ] && grep -q "Session › /start-session (v13) › POST /start-session" "$LOG_FILE"; then
      echo "Detected tr
title: Stabilize nightly e2e workflow by retrying transient `/start-session` failures once

author: Copilot
body_head:
The `publish` workflow failed at the NuGet push step with `401` because no API key was provided. This change aligns the workflow with NuGet trusted publishing by exchanging GitHub OIDC identity for a short-lived NuGet API key at runtime.

- **Authentication flow update**
  - Added a `NuGet/login@v1` step in `.github/workflows/publish.yml` to request a temporary NuGet API key via OIDC.
  - Wired the step output as the push credential.

- **Publish command update**
  - Updated `dotnet nuget push` to pass the ephemeral key explicitly with `--api-key`, replacing implicit/absent credential behavior.

```yaml
- name: NuGet login (OIDC → temp API key)
  id: nuget-login
  uses: NuGet/login@v1
  with:
    user: ${{ github.repository_owner }}

- name: Push to NuGet
  run: dotnet nuget push ./artifacts/*.nupkg \
    --api-key ${{ steps.nuget-login.outputs.NUGET_API_KEY }} \
    --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json \
    --skip-duplicate
```
title: Use NuGet trusted publishing OIDC token for package publish

# Description 📣

`infisical secrets set` echoed the full plaintext secret value back in its result table (`SECRET NAME | SECRET VALUE | STATUS`, e.g. rows ending in `SECRET CREATED`). This leaks freshly-set secrets into terminals, logs, and AI-agent transcripts — a user hit this when an agent's output filter (matching on `created`) captured the whole rows.

Since the caller just supplied these values, there is no reason to print them back. This masks the `SECRET VALUE` column by default in the table output:

```
before:  │ API_KEY │ sk-abc123... │ SECRET CREATED │
after:   │ API_KEY │ ******       │ SECRET CREATED │
```

- Default table output now shows `******` for non-empty values (empty stays empty).
- New `--show-values` flag opts back into the plaintext table when explicitly desired.
- `--output json/yaml/dotenv` behavior is unchanged (explicit machine-readable formats).

## Type ✨

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Improvement
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

# Tests 🛠️

```sh
go build ./packages/cmd/          # passes
gofmt -l packages/cmd/secrets.go  # clean
infisical secrets set FOO=bar     # value now rendered as ******
infisical secrets set FOO=bar --show-v
title: fix(secrets set): mask secret values in output table by default

author: Copilot
body_head:
Dependabot reported multiple high/moderate vulnerabilities on transitive `js-yaml` entries in `package-lock.json` (merge-key CPU amplification, `!!omap` quadratic behavior/CVE-2026-59870 gap in older lines, and merge-related prototype pollution/DoS patterns). This change removes vulnerable lockfile resolution by pinning all dependency paths to a patched `js-yaml` line.

- **What changed**
  - Added an npm override in `package.json` to force a patched `js-yaml` version across the full dependency graph.
  - Regenerated `package-lock.json` so transitive paths stop resolving to vulnerable 3.x/early 4.x variants and converge on a patched 4.x release.

- **Dependency policy update**
  - Centralized transitive remediation through `overrides` instead of touching unrelated direct dependencies.
  - Keeps future installs deterministic and aligned with the patched `js-yaml` line unless explicitly changed.

```json
{
  "overrides": {
    "js-yaml": "^4.1.1"
  }
}
```
title: Force patched js-yaml resolution to clear Dependabot alerts in package-lock

**1. `connect-chatgpt` failed after a successful token exchange**

author: Copilot
body_head:
Series were dropping off the "Series Updates" row 30 days after they *first appeared* rather than 30 days after their *most recent* issue was added, so adding a new issue to a recently-created series didn't refresh its window.

### Root cause
`OverviewService.BuildSeriesUpdates` gated eligibility on the series' first-added timestamp:

```csharp
e.LatestCreatedAt >= cutoff && e.EarliestCreatedAt < cutoff
```

The `EarliestCreatedAt < cutoff` clause locked out any series whose first issue was within the last 30 days. Such series only appeared under "Newly Added" — whose lifetime is tied to first-appearance — so a new issue never refreshed the 30-day window.

### Changes
- **`OverviewService.BuildSeriesUpdates`** — replace the first-added gate with a last-added one:

  ```csharp
  e.LatestCreatedAt >= cutoff && e.EarliestCreatedAt < e.LatestCreatedAt
  ```

  Retention now keys off `LatestCreatedAt`, so adding an issue refreshes the 30-day window regardless of when the series first appeared. The `EarliestCreatedAt < LatestCreatedAt` guard keeps a brand-new series with only its initial issue(s) out of Updates (it stays in Newly Added), while admitting any series — new or old — that has
title: Retain Series Updates for 30 days from last update, not first-added date

`DistributedTransactionCoordinator::percolatorCommit()` skipped the prepare/vote round entirely, allowing write-skew under `SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION`: two concurrent transactions could each read a consistent snapshot, write to disjoint shards, and both commit without any conflict being detected. ### `src/sharding/distributed_transaction.cpp` — Core fix
`percolatorCommit()` now runs `preparePhase()` before assigning the commit timestamp. On any ABORT vote, it sends ABORT to all already-prepared participants and returns false. The commit timestamp / commit-wait / COMMIT sequence only proceeds after a clean prepare round.

After:   percolatorCommit → preparePhase (vote) → assign commit_ts → commit-wait → COMMIT
                                ↓ on any ABORT vote
                            sendAbort(prepared participants) → return false
```

author: Copilot
body_head:
The `validate-and-render` job was failing with HTTP 403 on the "Post PR comment" step whenever a PR came from a fork. GitHub silently restricts `GITHUB_TOKEN` to read-only for `pull_request` events from forks, regardless of what `permissions:` declares.

## Changes

- **`pull_request` → `pull_request_target`** — runs in the base-repo context, so declared `issues: write` / `pull-requests: write` permissions are always honoured, including for fork PRs.
- **Explicit `ref: head.sha` on checkout** — `pull_request_target` defaults to checking out the base branch; this restores the PR's actual content.
- **New "Restore trusted scripts" step** — immediately after checkout, all executable paths (`scripts/`, `templates/`, `template.yaml`, `paths.yml`, `index.html`, `theme.css`) are overwritten from the base branch SHA. Only lesson YAML *data* files from the fork remain, and they are only parsed, never executed.

```yaml
- name: Checkout PR content
  uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
    fetch-depth: 0

- name: Restore trusted scripts and config from base branch
  run: |
    git fetch origin ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
    git c
title: Fix validate-and-render: switch to pull_request_target for fork PR write access

The quiet-quit term cannot carry cruelty-caused disengagement — the committed sweep shows the kind room quiet-quits 5× more while the cruel room's disengagement lands in desertions (1.97 vs 0.03/match) and churned careers. author: Copilot
body_head:
The `buildx` failure came from resolving `AGENTMEMORY_VERSION` to a non-existent npm version (`ETARGET` on `@agentmemory/agentmemory@0.9.29`). The workflow logic was deriving `latest + 1 patch` instead of using a published version.

- **Version resolution logic**
  - Updated both agentmemory build workflows to use `npm view @agentmemory/agentmemory version` directly when no manual version input is provided.
  - Removed patch auto-increment behavior that could generate unpublished versions.

- **Workflow UX alignment**
  - Updated `workflow_dispatch` input descriptions to reflect actual behavior: “leave blank to use latest published npm version”.

- **Scope**
  - `.github/workflows/build-agentmemory.yml`
  - `.github/workflows/build-agentmemory-mcp-all.yml`

```yaml
# before
CURRENT=$(npm view @agentmemory/agentmemory version 2>/dev/null || echo "0.9.26")
VERSION="${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.$((PATCH + 1))"

# after
VERSION=$(npm view @agentmemory/agentmemory version 2>/dev/null || echo "0.9.26")
```
title: Use published `@agentmemory/agentmemory` version in build workflows

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Summary

Splits Karry into three deployable services while keeping specialist agent clones inside the main backend:

```text
karry-agent   -> app:app         (brain + APIs)
karry-monitor -> device_app:app  KARRY_DEVICE_ROLE=monitor
karry-worker  -> device_app:app  KARRY_DEVICE_ROLE=worker
```

`device_app.py` is a shared role shell that serves only its own page and proxies `/api/autonomy/*` to `KARRY_BACKEND_URL`. It requires HTTPS outside localhost, allowlists headers, and caps request bodies at 700 KiB. Android and iOS can now point monitor and worker builds at separate URLs.

Also adds opt-in background location history for `KarryOperator`:

- iOS: a visible toggle starts `startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges()` once iOS **Always** permission is granted, and it keeps recording after the app closes. Turning the toggle off, unenrolling, or revoking the permission stops it.
- Backend: `POST /api/mobile-agent/devices/{id}/location` (operation token only). History is available through the owner route and through the observer route scoped to that device. Data is kept for 30 days and capped at 1,000 points per read.
- When `DATABASE_URL` is set, points are stored in PostgreSQL
title: Split monitor/worker deployments and add opt-in location history

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
closes #23169

this PR makes `upload_bundle_to_azure_blob_storage` pass `overwrite=True` so repeated and concurrent uploads of a content-addressed `include_files` sidecar (`files/<sha256>.zip`) no longer fail with `ResourceExistsError`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `ZipBuilder` intentionally reuses the same key for identical included content, but the Azure uploader used Azure's default no-overwrite `upload_blob`, so a second (or concurrent) submission with the same files failed before the flow ran. The S3 and GCS uploaders already overwrite by default, as do the other Azure upload paths in this package (`deployments/steps.py`, `AzureBlobStorageContainer.write_path`).
- Fixing it at the uploader means both the generic `.submit_to_work_pool()` path and the direct Docker path from #22858 get the same behavior.
- Tests: added a `FakeContainerClient` that enforces Azure's no-overwrite default, with coverage for a repeated upload and 5 concurrent uploads to the same key. The existing upload-error test now uses `ClientAuthenticationError` so it still verifies that unrelated failures propagate as `RuntimeError`.

Not reproduced against a live Azure account; verified with unit t
title: Make Azure bundle uploads idempotent for reused sidecar keys

Re-points the P10 determinism gate (`RuleBasedDispatcherDeterminismRunner`) at `DispatchTickLoop + RuleBasedEmissionStrategy` instead of the superseded `AgentLoopDriver + RuleBasedPlanAdapter`.

## New types

- **`ActionAuthor`** enum — distinguishes `RULE_BASED` (intentional rule run, stays `Running`) from `RULE_FALLBACK` (LLM mid-run failure, triggers `Failed`). Conflating them would mark every P10 gate run as `FAILED`.
- **`RunOutcome`** sealed interface — `Running` / `Completed` / `Failed(reason)` backed by `TerminalFallbackGuard`.
- **`EmissionStrategy`** fun interface — pluggable decide seam; `emit(prompt, obs): List<AttributedAction>?`
- **`TickBudget`** interface — `DeadlineTickBudget` (LLM) and `NoTimeoutBudget` (rule-based).
- **`TerminalFallbackGuard`** — transitions outcome to `Failed(LLM_ABANDONED)` on the first `RULE_FALLBACK` action; `RULE_BASED` is never a trigger.

## New classes

**`DispatchTickLoop`** — core loop: sense → annotate → render → emit (budgeted) → validate → ac

This PR is about reproducing the browser tab crash during long async (mailbox) games, not fixing it. The crash now reproduces reliably. The app code is unchanged, and the bugs found are filed as issues.

```sh
npm run bundle && cd e2e && npm ci
node chaos.js --scenario turns --seed 41 --steps 20 --fill-storage-kb 3500 --heap-mb 512
# FAIL turns mailbox seed 41: … CRASH: B's tab crashed during turn 13: B comes back   (exit 2)
```

That command crashed a tab for seeds 41, 7 and 3, each 47–65 s into the run. Without pre-filled storage the crash comes around game index 140 with a 512 MB heap cap, and after 6–7 min at Chrome's default heap.

### Crash mechanism
Covered in detail in `issues/open/2026-11-07-browser-crash-storage-error-chat-loop.md`:
1. **Chat is the game log.** Every play appends a `PlayMadeMessage` holding the full `Game` (~50–80 kB of JSON), with no cap on most paths.
2. **Async play saves it constantly.** `notify` calls `saveChat` on every catch-up, so a long game pushes `room/<room>/chat` past Chrome's 5,242,880-char localStorage quota.
3. **The error embeds the value twice**, once in the `setItem` FFI and again in `saveStorage`.
4. **The error feeds itself.** `logErr
title: e2e: reproduce the async catch-up tab crash and file browser-crash issues

This PR updates the release pipeline to use npm Trusted Publishers instead of token-based npm authentication. It aligns `release.yaml` with npm’s GitHub Actions OIDC flow now that npm-side trusted publishing is already configured.

- **Release auth model**
  - Enables OIDC for the publish job by granting `id-token: write`.
  - Removes npm token environment variables from the Changesets publish step (`NPM_TOKEN`, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`).

- **Permission scoping**
  - Applies required permissions at the `publish` job level (not workflow-wide) to keep privilege scope tight while preserving Changesets GitHub operations.

```yaml
jobs:
  publish:
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Create Release Pull Request or Publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```
title: Configure npm trusted publishing in release workflow (GitHub OIDC)

author: Copilot
body_head:
The `Update Coding Activity` GitHub Actions job was failing because `athul/waka-readme` received repeated `403 FORBIDDEN` responses from the WakaTime API and exited non-zero. This PR keeps the workflow informative while preventing transient/external WakaTime authorization failures from failing the scheduled run.

- **Failure containment in workflow step**
  - Added an explicit step id for the WakaTime action.
  - Set `continue-on-error: true` on the WakaTime update step so external API access failures do not fail the entire job.

- **Explicit degraded-path signal**
  - Added a conditional warning step that runs only when the WakaTime step fails, making skipped updates visible in job logs.

```yaml
- id: update-wakatime
  uses: athul/waka-readme@v0.2.5
  continue-on-error: true
  with:
    WAKATIME_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.WAKATIME_API_KEY }}
    SHOW_TITLE: true
    TIME_RANGE: last_7_days
    LANG_COUNT: 6
    SHOW_TIME: true
    SHOW_TOTAL: true
    BLOCKS: "░▒▓█"

- name: WakaTime update skipped
  if: steps.update-wakatime.outcome == 'failure'
  run: echo "::warning::WakaTime API returned 403/forbidden; skipping README coding activity update for this run."
```
title: Make Update Coding Activity resilient to WakaTime API 403 failures

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Summary

The extension could not compile, let alone play anything: `custom.ts` called `music.createSoundBuffer` / `music.playSoundBuffer`, neither of which exists in Arcade (verified against pxt-arcade 4.2.1 — the build fails with `Property 'playSoundBuffer' does not exist on type 'typeof music'`). Arcade has no sample playback engine at all; the only low-level audio API is `music.playInstructions`, which plays tones described by `(waveform, frequency, duration, startVolume, endVolume, endFrequency)`.

So PCM is now re-synthesised rather than "played". `analyze()` cuts the samples into 10ms frames and, per frame, estimates pitch from the zero-crossing rate (with a hysteresis guard so noise around the centre line isn't counted) and loudness from peak amplitude; each frame becomes one 12-byte instruction ramped towards the next frame's pitch/volume to avoid clicks. Instructions are queued 8 at a time, never more than 200ms ahead of playback — the same pacing `MelodyPlayer` uses — so long clips don't overflow the mixer queue.

```
frame -> hz = crossings * rate / (2 * frameSamples), volume = peak * 8   // peak 0-127 -> 0-1024

title: Make the PCM audio extension compile and actually play sound

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Summary

GitHub's shared scheduler starts this workflow late — the last 20 runs began 74 to 197 minutes after their cron — so the "11:00 / 17:00 Central" schedule actually lands closer to 13:00 / 19:00. Moving each cron an hour earlier puts the typical start back near the intended times.

```diff
-    - cron: "0 16 * * *"   # 11:00 CDT      -> morning
-    - cron: "0 17 * * *"   # 11:00 CST
-    - cron: "0 22 * * *"   # 17:00 CDT      -> evening
-    - cron: "0 23 * * *"   # 17:00 CST
+    - cron: "0 15 * * *"   # 10:00 CDT
+    - cron: "0 16 * * *"   # 10:00 CST
+    - cron: "0 21 * * *"   # 16:00 CDT
+    - cron: "0 22 * * *"   # 16:00 CST
```

The `gate` job's `morning`/`evening` strings move with them, so it still keeps exactly one morning and one evening cron per DST offset and drops the other two. Note the CST morning slot is now `0 16 * * *`, which used to be the CDT morning slot; since the gate only ever compares against the pair for the *current* offset, that reuse is harmless.

Nothing about the data changes: the 14-day rolling window and `inspection_id` merge make the exact start time irrelevant to completeness.


Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d
title: Shift the scrape crons an hour earlier to absorb GitHub's scheduler delay

The 0.11.0 performance record against v0.10.1 (#1337) leaves one regression after #1348: the language server's `ReferencesCold` (44 ms → ~1.0 s, 9.8 MiB → ~950 MiB per query) and `RenameWarm` (20 ms → ~1.7 s, 1.4 MiB → ~1.5 GiB), bisected by exact allocation counts to #1062 (hidden colliding imports). #1348 removed the per-member garbage; what remains is the member lists themselves, rebuilt over and over: since #1062 made enumerating what a wildcard import surfaces expensive, every document a references query indexes and every occurrence a rename rewrites enumerated the same imports again. author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body_head:
## Summary

Adds the missing `GlobalMessage` display rule to `CheckoutAppearanceRules` in the Swift checkout SDK.

The embedded-checkout backend and the web/JS SDK already support `GlobalMessage: { display: "visible" | "hidden" }` (gated in Paella-Labs/crossbit-main#27986 and Crossmint/crossmint-sdk#1991 for PAY-12564). The Swift checkout SDK was still omitting the field when serializing `appearance` into the checkout URL, so iOS clients could not use the new rule to surface global error messages (e.g. Sardine/Google Pay rejections) in the express-checkout tabs.

## Changes

- Introduce `CheckoutGlobalMessageRule` with a nullable `display` string.
- Add `globalMessage: CheckoutGlobalMessageRule?` to `CheckoutAppearanceRules`, serialized as `GlobalMessage`.
- Add a regression test verifying the generated checkout URL contains the new rule.

## Test plan

- `swift build` / `swift test` could not be run locally because the installed Swift toolchain is 6.0.3 while `Package.swift` requires 6.2.0; CI should build and test on the PR.
- CI should run the new `urlContainsAppearanceGlobalMessageRule` test.

## Related

- PAY-12564
- Paella-Labs/crossbit-main#27986
- Crossmint/crossmint-sdk#1
title: fix(Models): add GlobalMessage display rule to CheckoutAppearanceRules

## Summary

Owners can now talk to their Allagio account from Telegram — a real channel, not a demo shim. `TelegramRunner` long-polls the Bot API (`getUpdates`, 25 s hold) as a background worker and answers `/start` `/help` `/link CODE` `/status` `/earnings` `/unlink`, with `/status` and `/earnings` rendering the same `AccountDigest` the weekly email uses. No `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` → no runner, no DMs, zero change in behavior.

Linking is one-time-code based: `/owner/settings` gains a Telegram section where the owner generates a code (`POST /owner/telegram/code`, shown once via `?tg=` flash), then sends `/link CODE` to the bot. Codes store only their SHA-256 (`owner_telegram_codes`, migration `064_owner_telegram.sql`), expire in 15 min, are single-use (`DELETE ... RETURNING`), and are replaced when a new one is issued. `owners.telegram_chat_id` / `telegram_username` hold the binding; `/owner/telegram/unlink` clears it.

The "wow" half: a linked chat also gets direct messages for the three events the owner webhook already fires — `deal.waiting` (`orp_notify`), `assessment.finished` (`assessments`), `account.registered` (`agent_entry`) — via a shared `telegramDM` helper, and DMs fire e

author: lukepiette
body_head:
## Problem

Hub template **v2.27.0** (bundles vLLM **v0.29.0**) fails **~31%** of first requests vs ~10–11% on v2.26.0 (vLLM 0.28.0). Worker-log analysis of 50 failed v2.27.0 endpoints shows **88% "Revision Not Found"**: since v0.28 vLLM resolves every HF ref to an exact commit hash at launch (upstream's fix for [Artifact Pin Decay, GHSA-3ww4-5jv9-j5gm](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-3ww4-5jv9-j5gm) — so upstream won't restore main-fallback). A force-pushed repo invalidates the pinned hash → `RevisionNotFoundError`. Worse, **v0.29.0 ships huggingface_hub 1.28.0, which leaks a resolved pin across repos** (model repo's hash applied to the tokenizer/weights repo → guaranteed 404); fixed upstream only in vllm [#56092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56092) + hf_hub ≥ 1.30. The engine rollback for that class is #344; this PR is the worker-side hardening that helps on every engine version.

## What this PR does

1. **`main.py` — one relaunch for vanished revisions.** When startup dies on `RevisionNotFoundError`, relaunch `vllm serve` once: every launch re-resolves the pin, so this genuinely recovers the force-push case. Explicit `MODEL_REVISION`/`
title: Recover vanished HF revisions at startup and classify them correctly

author: thpr
body_head:
## Summary

Checking off a conflict-of-interest (COI) flag in `packages/expense` now refuses anyone who signed a line on the expense, or is in a signer's household.

A COI flag is raised by a sign-off: a Board member filling the Treasurer seat because no finance holder could sign, or a card charge that needs a second Board substitution. The existing check already refuses the submitter, the reimbursee and their households. It did not refuse the Board member whose own sign-off raised the flag, so that person could check it off themselves.

The rule is deliberately broader than "the signer who raised the flag": the flag does not record which sign-off raised it, and the checkoff should come from an independent reviewer anyway. So **every** signer on the expense, and everyone in a signer's household, is refused. A Board member who did not sign and is not in a signer's household can still check the flag off.

Only COI flags get the signer check; other flag kinds are unchanged.

## Not in this PR

The matching receipt-side fix (finance-tier edits on one's own receipt; date edits after review) lives in the receipt library and waits on #1973. It will follow in a separate PR once #1973 lands
title: fix(expense): a signer cannot check off a conflict-of-interest flag

author: mbryzek
body_head:
Adopts prettier 3.9.6 in `abundantnexus`, so this repo's formatter matches the rest of the SvelteKit family.

`package.json` declares `^3.9.4`, so 3.9.6 was already inside the declared range and only the committed lock was holding it back. A formatter rewrites source, so while the family's locks disagree the same file formats differently from repo to repo — and the gap lands as a surprise reformat inside whichever unrelated pull request regenerates a lock next.

Target for the family: prettier **3.9.6** and prettier-plugin-tailwindcss **0.8.1** — the newest already in the family and the newest published. `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` is already at 0.8.1 here, so only prettier moves.

**Diff is the lockfile only.** `prettier --check .` is clean both before and after the bump in this repo, so nothing under `src/` changes.

Verified locally on a clean clone of `origin/main`: `npm ci` → `npx prettier --check .` clean → `npm update prettier prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` → `npx prettier --check .` clean → `npm run check` passes.

Part of epic [ISS-4405]; re-measure the family with `dev dependencies policy`.

author: mschwartzen
body_head:
## Problem

The forms list finds Elementor forms placed directly on a page, or placed through a Global Widget. It misses a form inside a saved template that is embedded with the **Template widget** or the **`[elementor-template id="N"]` shortcode**. Those forms never reach the SaaS, which then refuses to create a flow: `Form plugin "elementor" not found on this WordPress site`.

Live case: skyhighcannabis.ca. The homepage (page 29) embeds template 28 with a Template widget, and the contact form `6829844c` lives in that template. Its flow had to be created by swapping parameters in the prod DB.

## The id rule

| How the form is placed | Rendered `form_id` |
| --- | --- |
| Directly on a page | the form element's id |
| Global Widget | the **host page's** element id (unchanged, already handled) |
| Template widget / shortcode | the **template's** form element id, the same on every page |

Confirmed on Sky High: the form posts `form_id=6829844c`, `post_id=28` (the template), `queried_id=29` (the page).

## Changes

- `checkview_scan_elementor_elements()`: walks one element tree and returns its own forms (Global Widgets resolved as before) plus the template ids it embeds via the Templ
title: fix(api): discover Elementor forms inside embedded templates

author: bluevulpine
body_head:
## Problem

The gitea image bump opens **two** Renovate PRs for a single update (this sweep: #1540 `docker.io/gitea/gitea` and #1541 `gitea/gitea`). gitea is a real Helm chart with a top-level `image.repository`/`image.tag` that the **helm-values** manager tracks natively, and the tag line *also* carries a `# renovate:` annotation that the **customManager** tracks — both match the same line.

An `overrides.json5` packageRule already existed to suppress the helm-values copy, but it **never fired**: it matched the exact packageName `docker.io/gitea/gitea`, while Renovate normalizes the Docker Hub name to the un-prefixed `gitea/gitea`.

## Fix

Match by regex `/gitea\/gitea$/`, which catches the packageName with or without the `docker.io/` registry prefix. Still scoped to `matchManagers: ["helm-values"]`, so it can only disable the helm-values duplicate — never the annotation-based customManager PR we keep. Stale comment (claimed a nonexistent `registry: docker.io` field) corrected.

Validated with `renovate-config-validator` (no errors on this rule).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: fix(renovate): actually dedupe the gitea double-PR (regex packageName match)

author: ybyesilyurt
body_head:
## Summary

The lyrics agent's Genius search misses ~all YouTube-sourced tracks because yt-dlp passes the raw video title verbatim. Real-world repro from prod just now:

- Track: `The Weeknd - Can't Feel My Face` (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KEI4qSrkPAs)
- Genius search query built: `"The Weeknd - Can't Feel My Face (Official Video) The Weeknd"`
- Top Genius hit returned: **"The Weeknd Rolling Stones Interview"**
- Result: `source=whisper_only`, mediocre transcription

With the cleaned query `"Can't Feel My Face The Weeknd"`, Genius returns the correct song first.

## Fix

`_build_search_query()` cleans the title before search:
1. Strip `"Artist - "` prefix when the artist field is already known
2. Strip parenthetical/bracketed noise: `(Official Video)`, `[Audio]`, `(HD)`, `[Lyrics]`, `(Live)`, etc.
3. Keep `(feat. X)` — that's part of the canonical title
4. Collapse whitespace + trim stray hyphens

## Files
- `src/apps/api/app/services/genius_client.py` — new `_build_search_query()` helper + noise-tag regex
- `src/apps/api/tests/services/test_genius_client.py` — 6 new tests covering YouTube title patterns + edge cases

## Test plan
- [x] 15/15 genius_client tests pass locally
title: fix(lyrics): strip YouTube title noise before Genius search

author: alistair3149
body_head:
## Problem

Dependabot cannot propose this bump itself: codesniffer `51.0.0` exact-pins `squizlabs/php_codesniffer 3.13.5`, which is blocked by security advisory GHSA-hmqg-cxww-wqhq (CVE-2026-67434, [T434187](https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T434187)) — its resolver refuses advisory-affected versions while resolving the *current* manifest, so every composer update job dies before it can compute the fix.

## Behaviour

`52.0.0` moves the pin to the patched PHPCS 3.13.6, clearing the advisory and unblocking future Dependabot composer runs. Verified in Docker: `composer update` resolves cleanly and `composer test` passes with no new sniff findings.

Same change as StarCitizenTools/mediawiki-skins-Citizen#1758, applied across the maintained repos.

## Merge order

**Requires StarCitizenTools/mediawiki-ci-workflows#18 first** — codesniffer 52 requires PHP ≥ 8.3, so the REL1_43/analyze legs fail until that matrix change lands on `main`. Re-run this PR's CI after it merges.

author: OikuraSodachi
body_head:
Closes #348

## 원인
FTP 목록에서 해석하지 못한 줄은 **그 목록의 상태**인데, `FtpPathAwareFileSystem`이 조회할 때마다 일회성 알림(Snackbar)으로 넣었다. 그래서 새로고침할 때마다 같은 알림이 알림함에 쌓였다.

Part of #550. Found by the operator: the window printed `NICKin #channel` where it should say `NICK in #channel`, on every REQUEST, QUEUED, SENDING, SENT, FAIL and SEARCH line.

`dccore.in` (added with the channel in the feed, #574) returned `$+($chr(32),in,$chr(32),$1)`, so its result began with a space - and mIRC drops leading spaces from what an alias returns. `$2 $+ $dccore.in($3)` then joined the nick and "in" directly. author: markwpearce
body_head:
Fixes #529
Fixes #533

Fog now fixes the draw distance: with fog on, the camera draws to `maxDrawDistance` at every quality level, so the fog edge, skyline and fades never move when quality changes. Walls and models fade the same, nothing pops to fog when it redraws, and the skyline stops shrinking. `Fog.followsQuality` opts back in to the old behaviour, eased over `qualityTransitionSeconds` (4s) so it creeps instead of jumping. Same idea as other engines - view distance is a player setting in Unreal, and Unity only shrinks it alongside thicker fog.

Replaces the earlier "keep cached images" approach (reverted in this PR) - it fixed models but not walls, and kept buildings snapped to fog when they went stale. Design in `specs/2026-11-15-fog-fixed-distance-design.md`.

Device, town at default spawn (old distances via `draw=`):
- Basic still 50.1 fps vs 57.7, orbiting 12.0 vs 13.3
- Ultra still 45.2 vs 38.7, orbiting 4.4 vs 3.9

Winning back Basic's ~10% is #534.

author: Osasuwu
body_head:
Closes #174

## What

*Trigger configuration* gains **Where likes go**, a core like setting sitting with the other like settings (not a fourth entry under *Extra actions* — this is what a like *is*, not something that happens after one):

- **Liked songs** — the service's own like. The default, and what every existing install keeps doing.
- **A playlist** — a playlist of yours, named by hand.
- **Both**.

The playlist is matched **by name on whichever service played the song**, and created on first use, so one name works on both Spotify and YouTube Music. The UI says so, and on YouTube Music it also carries the quota note: a playlist write costs ≈50 of the 10,000 daily units, the same as a like.

## Why the playlist leg matters most on YouTube Music

Spotify has Liked Songs *and* playlists; YouTube Music's thumbs-up is one bucket with no second one. Anyone sorting their music by hand had nowhere for a triggered like to land.

## Not drifting across three like paths

A like happens in three places — the in-app button, the headphone trigger, and the Kotlin `SpotifyLikeWorker` that runs while the app is asleep. Each language now has exactly one pure type that decides which legs run an

author: ParagonJenko
body_head:
## Fix the Dependency Audit failure

`pnpm audit --audit-level high` (the **Dependency Audit** CI job) was failing on two HIGH advisories:

| Package | Vulnerable | Patched | Advisory | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nodemailer` | `<=9.0.0` | `>=9.0.1` | [GHSA-p6gq-j5cr-w38f](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p6gq-j5cr-w38f) — message-level `raw` option bypasses `disableFileAccess`/`disableUrlAccess` → arbitrary file read + SSRF | `services/notifications > nodemailer` |
| `undici` | `>=7.23.0 <7.28.0` | `>=7.28.0` | [GHSA-vmh5-mc38-953g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmh5-mc38-953g) — TLS certificate-validation bypass | `jsdom > undici` (apps' test toolchain) |

### Fix
Force both to patched versions via pnpm `overrides` and document each in `overridesDocumentation`:
- `"nodemailer@<9.0.1": "^9.0.1"`
- `"undici@>=7.23.0 <7.28.0": "^7.28.0"`

Overrides are the only clean fix for the **transitive** `undici` (pulled in by `jsdom`, which we don't depend on directly), and they're consistent with the existing `ws`/`esbuild` security overrides in this file.

### Safety
`services/notifications` uses only `createTransport` + `sendMail` — **not** the vulnerable `raw`
title: chore(security): patch nodemailer + undici high-severity advisories

author: stasson
body_head:
## Summary

Adopt the conventional dev-tool verb vocabulary (`fmt` / `check` / `lint`) and let the orchestration layer (git-std, `just`, CI) compose the gates instead of a bundled command.

- **`markspec format` → `markspec fmt`** — pure rename; flags (`--check`), args, and behavior unchanged.
- **`markspec validate` → `markspec check`** — pure rename; `--strict` / `--format` flags and diagnostics unchanged. `check` is the idiomatic correctness gate (cf. `cargo check`/`deno check`) and avoids the V-model "validation" overloading for the ISO 26262 / ASPICE audience.
- **`markspec hook` removed** — its three stages are already reachable as primitives (`fmt --check`, `check`, `lock --check`); git-std (`~`/`!`/`?` prefixes) or a `just` target composes them. The git-hooks recipe is rewritten around this (husky dropped — git-std replaces it).

**Deliberately unchanged:** the core `format()`/`validate()` library functions, the agent-facing MCP `validate` tool (named for its audience), the `--format` CLI flag, and `CHANGELOG.md` history.

Updated alongside the code: all e2e/unit tests, ~42 docs, the `skills/` bundle source, and `.claude/rules`.

Pre-1.0, no-backward-compat policy: hard ren

author: Botanicbox0
body_head:
## 무엇

대표 지시(2026-10-29): "랜딩의 이미지는 내가 편하게 수정할 수 있게(wix처럼) admin.twings.app에 랜딩 미디어 수정 기능".

`admin.twings.app/admin/landing-media`(메뉴: 콘텐츠 관리 → 랜딩 이미지)에서 랜딩 이미지를 칸 단위로 바꾸고 되돌린다. 배포는 필요 없다.

- **칸은 랜딩 순서대로 놓인다.** 브랜드 랜딩 탭에는 히어로 병, 무드 폴더, 무드 라이브러리·제품 컷, 생성 예시, 착용, 피드, 캠페인 서비스 사진이 있다. 개인 랜딩 탭에는 셀카 → 장면이 있다.
- **바꾸기**: 칸에 끌어다 놓거나 눌러서 고르면 바로 바뀐다. 칸에는 `교체됨` 배지가 붙고 랜딩 캐시(`/`, `/brands`, 태그 `landing-media`)도 같이 갱신된다.
- **기본으로**: 행을 지운다. 그러면 `public/`의 원래 파일이 다시 보인다.
- 한 파일은 쓰이는 모든 곳에서 한 칸이다. 예를 들어 `studio/smoke-1`을 바꾸면 무드 타일, 검색 칸, 메모리 썸네일이 함께 바뀐다.
- **영상과 그 포스터는 칸이 아니다.** 옛 영상 위에 새 포스터를 얹으면 보이는 것과 재생되는 것이 달라진다. 같은 이유로 홈 히어로의 장면 사진을 바꾸면 그 옛 영상은 빠진다.

## 어떻게

| 부분 | 파일 |
| --- | --- |
| 슬롯 레지스트리(83칸: 스튜디오 77, 서비스 사진 4, 셀카 → 장면 2) | `lib/content/landing-media.ts` |
| 행 읽기·URL 만들기 / 캐시된 투영(태그 + 1시간 TTL) | `lib/content/landing-media-repo.ts`, `lib/content/landing-media-server.ts` |
| 작업 `landingMedia.replace` / `landingMedia.reset`(`/admin/do`, 관리자 전용 인증 매트릭스에 자동 포함) | `lib/admin/landing-media-operations.ts` |
| 편집 화면 | `app/(admin)/admin/landing-media/page.tsx`, `components/admin/landing-media-editor.tsx` |
| 로컬 모드 이미지 경로(클라우드에서는 공개 버킷을 직접 링크) | `app/api/landing-media/[...slot]/route.ts` |
|

author: DrGarbitsch
body_head:
## Summary

Supersedes #808.

PR #808 fixed the `@type`-as-string case by replacing `String.prototype.includes()` with `=== `. However CodeQL still flagged the array branch because `Array.prototype.includes()` is also treated as a substring check by the `js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` rule.

This PR replaces all four `array.includes(url)` calls with `array.some(t => t === url)`, making the exact-match intent explicit for both branches:

- `GeoProperty` (alert #38)
- `JsonProperty` (alert #39)
- `ListProperty` / `Relationship` (alerts #40, #41)

All four instances follow the same pattern:

```js
// before
Array.isArray(refObj['@type']) && refObj['@type'].includes('https://uri.etsi.org/ngsi-ld/...')
// after
Array.isArray(refObj['@type']) && refObj['@type'].some(t => t === 'https://uri.etsi.org/ngsi-ld/...')
```

- [ ] CodeQL check passes with no new alerts on the changed lines
- [ ] K8s tests pass

author: JoNil
body_head:
A `for` over a direct `stdlib.iterator.range` or `range-inclusive` call now counts from the call's two arguments. It builds no range value and does not type the source as a whole. This is step 1b of the loop-migration plan: the lean range expansion that uses the callee-identity query (#8777) and the call-argument accessor (#8784), both now in stage0.

## The expansion

`(for [i (iterator.range s e)] body...)` becomes

```
(let [__for_index : i64 s] [__for_end : i64 e]
  (while (< __for_index __for_end)
    (let [i __for_index]
      (begin (set! __for_index (+ __for_index 1)) body... unit))))
```

- **Literal end.** When `e` is an integer literal, it is compared in place and `__for_end` is dropped.
- **`range-inclusive`.** The loop tests `index < last` before stepping, so a range that ends at the largest `i64` stops without stepping past it:

  ```
  (let [__for_index : i64 s] [__for_last : i64 e] [__for_more (<= __for_index __for_last)]
    (while __for_more
      (let [i __for_index] (begin (set! __for_more (< __for_index __for_last)) (set! __for_index (+ __for_index 1)) body... unit))))
  ```

- **When it applies.** Only to a single unannotated clause whose source `comptime.expr
title: for: count a direct stdlib.iterator.range call from its arguments

author: javierbq
body_head:
Closes #618. Part of #610.

## What this adds

The studio rig's air (`atmosphere haze=…, dust=…`, from #611/#612) is now drawn. It is a post pass of its own that runs after either pass 1 (RT on or off) and before the OIT resolve, DOF, outline and tonemap. Glass and transparent surfaces composite over it.

- **Haze:** forward-scattering beams. Henyey-Greenstein phase with g clamped to ±0.9 and capped at 5x. 48 jittered steps over a static density, so haze alone never animates.
- **Dust:** 32 depth layers of motes with drift, wobble and twinkle. They are lit only inside beams, take the colour of the light that reaches them, and are capped at 8x.
- **Shafts from every shadowed light.** The pass reads #616's shadow-map array and the `LightRigBlock` tail; there is no second shadow path. Motes call `light_shadow_lookup` verbatim. By default the haze takes one hardware compare per step (`post_air_shadow_tap`, which a test pins to the lookup's statements). `metal_light_air_shadow_filter 2` switches it to #616's 3x3. Before each lookup, an air sample is pulled back onto the light's far plane, so shafts reach past the caster sphere.
- **No air without geometry**, and none in grid mode. Every

author: daniel-thom
body_head:
## Summary
- Fixes the Jobs-tab Elapsed value ticking up indefinitely after a job completes.
- Root cause: `format_elapsed` used `Utc::now()` on every redraw (~100 ms), and the column only renders for `status == Running`. `app.jobs` only refreshes on manual `r`, post-popup, or the 30 s auto-refresh (off by default), so the locally-cached row stayed at `Running` and Elapsed kept growing.
- Capture `jobs_fetched_at` whenever `jobs_all` is loaded from the server and compute Elapsed relative to that snapshot. The value reflects "how long the job had been running as of the last refresh" and stops advancing on its own when the data goes stale.

## Test plan
- [ ] Run a workflow with a short-lived job in the TUI; confirm the Jobs tab's Elapsed value stops growing once the job is no longer Running on the server (verified after `r` clears the row, but in the meantime no longer ticks).
- [ ] Confirm Elapsed still updates after pressing `r` (or after auto-refresh fires) while a job is genuinely Running.
- [ ] Verify other Jobs-tab behavior is unchanged: filter, pagination, sort, popup-driven workflow runs.
